summary: Once someone accepts, the employer stops its search, so backing out later leaves a hole.
realLife: A career office points out that employers end their search after an acceptance, so withdrawing later wastes their time and can damage the candidate's reputation.
sources: UW-Madison SuccessWorks, accepting and negotiating your offer: https://successworks.wisc.edu/accepting-and-negotiating-your-offer/
inGame: Needs: a vacancy record that closes on acceptance; the jobs module's hire event can carry the closing. Scene: needs a producer for job-offer.

turns.summary: The employer keeps the second candidate warm in case the first backs out.
pulledBy: a vacancy that is hard to fill
turns.writesBack: The runner-up stays on a list, and the first candidate's backing out costs less.

turns.summary: The candidate backs out and the employer has to restart the whole search.
turns.writesBack: The employer's trust in the candidate falls, and the vacancy reopens.

turns.summary: The employer simply stops all searching and says nothing more to others.
turns.writesBack: The candidate's job record begins, and the other applicants hear nothing.
